## Comparability note

Four of the five carriers are directly comparable: all report calendar fiscal years (Jan 1–Dec 31) and the figures come from each company's FY2024 Form 10-K [DOC-1]. **Alaska Air Group is not directly comparable on an as-reported basis**: it closed the Hawaiian Holdings acquisition on September 18, 2024, and Hawaiian's results are consolidated from that date forward [DOC-2]. Alaska's FY2024 reported revenue therefore includes ~3.5 months of Hawaiian, while FY2022 and FY2023 do not.

Per the instruction, Alaska is shown **excluding the acquired business**, using the $869 million of Hawaiian revenue recognized from the acquisition date to December 31, 2024 [DOC-2]: $11,735M − $869M = **$10,866M** adjusted FY2024 revenue. (This is an approximation — it removes only the revenue Alaska separately identified as Hawaiian's, and does not adjust for any intercompany or network effects.)

## Ranking 1: FY2023 → FY2024 revenue growth

| Rank | Airline | FY2023 | FY2024 | Growth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | United | $53,717M | $57,063M | **+6.23%** [DOC-1] |
| 2 | Delta | $58,048M | $61,643M | **+6.19%** [DOC-1] |
| 3 | Southwest | $26,091M | $27,483M | **+5.34%** [DOC-1] |
| 4 | Alaska (ex-Hawaiian) | $10,426M | $10,866M | **+4.22%** [DOC-1][DOC-2] |
| 5 | American | $52,788M | $54,211M | **+2.70%** [DOC-1] |

United and Delta are effectively tied (a ~4 basis-point gap); the ordering between them is not robust to small adjustments. Alaska's *as-reported* growth would have been +12.56%, first place — the ranking change is entirely attributable to the Hawaiian acquisition [DOC-2].

## Ranking 2: FY2022 → FY2024 revenue growth

| Rank | Airline | FY2022 | FY2024 | Growth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | United | $44,955M | $57,063M | **+26.93%** [DOC-1] |
| 2 | Delta | $50,582M | $61,643M | **+21.87%** [DOC-1] |
| 3 | Southwest | $23,814M | $27,483M | **+15.41%** [DOC-1] |
| 4 | Alaska (ex-Hawaiian) | $9,646M | $10,866M | **+12.65%** [DOC-1][DOC-2] |
| 5 | American | $48,971M | $54,211M | **+10.70%** [DOC-1] |

## Conclusion

Yes — **United Airlines Holdings ranks first in both periods**, though its FY2023→FY2024 lead over Delta is within rounding-level significance, whereas its FY2022→FY2024 lead (~5 percentage points) is decisive. The full ordering is otherwise identical across both periods (United, Delta, Southwest, Alaska, American).

ANSWER: Yes — United is top-ranked in both. FY23→FY24: United +6.23%, Delta +6.19%, Southwest +5.34%, Alaska (ex-Hawaiian) +4.22%, American +2.70%. FY22→FY24: United +26.93%, Delta +21.87%, Southwest +15.41%, Alaska (ex-Hawaiian) +12.65%, American +10.70%. (Alaska adjusted to remove the $869M of Hawaiian revenue consolidated after the Sept 18, 2024 acquisition; United's 2024 lead over Delta is only ~4bps.)
